_comment: spec/target-spec.md 'Startup' row: release from vdd = 0, all 5 process corners x -40/27/125 C x 3 supplies, time to settle inside the band. 45 points.

WHY THIS BENCH EXISTS IN THIS TREE. The row's planned testbench is the inherited sim/sg13cmos5l-closed-loop-startup at the commit in reuse.lock.json. That bench recorded 45/45 points SELF-STARTING (source record 20260829-085039-94869af) but never extracted a settling TIME: every one of its measurements is a `.meas ... find ... at=` card at 20 us or at the 2 ms end point, so the row's `< 1 ms` has no evidence behind it anywhere. Extracting it needs a measurement the source bench does not have, so decision record 0011 supersedes the planned bench for this row with this one. The fixture (200 us ramp, 2 ms window, rshunt/gmin) and the three self-starting criteria are carried over unchanged, so the trajectory is the source's; what is added is t_settle_s.

THE BAND. `< 1 ms` names no band, so this bench states one and grades it: t_settle_s is the last instant at which |vref(t) - vref(2 ms)| exceeded 1% of vref(2 ms), measured from t = 0 (the release from vdd = 0), so it INCLUDES the 200 us supply ramp. A tighter band or a start taken from vdd-valid would both be easier to pass; this is the conservative reading of the row.

`analysis.linearize` resamples the transient onto a uniform 2 us grid before the expressions run, so t_settle_s has a deterministic 2 us resolution instead of depending on where the solver happened to step. Every measurement here is an `expr` over those linearized vectors -- no `.meas` cards -- so all of them read the same grid.

SELF-STARTING, as the source bench defined it (its record's Claim paragraph), all three graded here: the startup circuit releases (det_release_ratio = v(xdut.xx3.det)/v(vdd) <= 0.2), the real amplifier closes the loop (dvsns_v = |sns1 - sns2| <= 20 mV), and fb settles to an interior equilibrium rather than railing (fb_headroom_v = min(fb, vdd - fb) >= 0.05 V). vref_start_v is recorded to show the release really was from zero.

`corners.supply_waveforms` rescales the deck's PWL ramp per supply point (peak -> the corner's supply) instead of `alter`ing it, which ngspice cannot do to a waveform source. That is what lets one request carry the whole 45-point grid where the source bench needed one request per supply.

PORTABLE BY CONSTRUCTION: nothing here is a path that exists only on the submitting host, so this one request serves `--backend local` (a single-corner probe, narrowed by hand) and `--backend batch` (the grid sim/grid-run.sh submits).

- `models.pdk` selects the variant and the fleet's batch image (klayout-tools#2727 publishes sg13cmos5l). Each corner names its own PDK-relative section libraries, so no `models.lib` and no generated corner bundle is needed; an absolute host path here would be refused on batch (`models_lib_host_path`).

- `options.stage_model_inputs` ships THIS host's pinned model libraries and their whole `.include`/`.lib` closure with the job, so the models that ran are bound by sha256 to sim/pdk.json's pinned revision (`environment.staged_model_inputs` and `remote.runner_model_inputs` both list them) instead of being whatever the fleet image happens to carry. The image's own SG13CMOS5L tree publishes no readable revision stamp (`worker_environment.pdk.stamp_text` is null), so without staging the grid could not be bound to the pin at all -- see the bench README.

- `options.osdi_preload` entries are written as literal `$PDK_ROOT/...`, so they are runner-resolved off-host and expanded from the environment locally. They are NOT staged: the compact-model BINARIES are the executing image's. That residual gap is stated in the bench README.

- `netlist` is the deck sim/grid-run.sh generates under sim/build/ (gitignored); the runner substitutes an absolute path, and klt's include-closure staging uploads the migrated DUT the deck `.include`s. The relative default below is where the generated deck lands, so `klt sim --dry-run` works from the repo root once a runner has written it.
Process labels map to model sections exactly as the spec/target-spec.md §PVT table does: pnpMPA has no skew section, so sf and fs read cornerPNP/cornerRES `typ`.
`netlist_source` is `schematic`: the DUT is the xschem-exported netlist migrated by decision record 0006, not an extracted one.

LIMITS ARE THE RATIFIED TARGET COLUMN, the same rule the other four benches now follow (decision record 0011 §2). The 'Startup' row's Target is 'self-starting, < 1 ms' and its Fallback is 'self-starting' with no time at all, so the row's only numeric bound is the Target's: t_settle_s < 1 ms. The three self-starting measurements express the qualitative 'self-starting' that both columns share. No bound is edited either way.
